ticker_news.title: What's Next For US GDP Amid Iran Conflict
ticker_news.description: The US economy faces headwinds from the Iran conflict, with crude oil prices spiking to $118 and inflation expected to reach 4.2%. JPMorgan's chief economist forecasts zero Fed rate cuts in 2026 and a potential hike in Q3 2027. While unemployment fell to 4.3% and March job additions exceeded expectations at 178,000, earlier job losses and supply chain disruptions pose challenges. US manufacturing may benefit from Trump's protectionist policies and AI-driven innovations, but the economy's direction largely depends on resolving the Middle East conflict.
ticker_news.author: Dmytro Spilka

ticker_news.title: Why FMC Rallied in March, Even As Markets Fell
ticker_news.description: FMC Corporation rallied 16.8% in March despite a challenging 2025 due to two main factors: the Iran war creating a supply crunch in agricultural chemicals, and CEO announcements that 5-10 parties are interested in acquiring the company. However, the stock remains risky given high debt levels, industry cyclicality, and uncertain earnings impact from the supply crunch.
ticker_news.author: Billy Duberstein

SPY.title: Stock Market Today: S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures Surge As Trump Declares Ceasefire On Iran Strikes— SoFi, Uber, Levi Strauss In Focus  (UPDATED)
SPY.description: U.S. stock futures surged on Wednesday following President Trump's announcement of a two-week ceasefire on Iran strikes. Major indices posted strong gains with the S&P 500 up 2.46%, Nasdaq 100 up 3.25%, and Russell 2000 up 3.59%. However, analyst Jeremy Siegel warns of near-term caution despite long-term bullish outlook, citing labor strength, inflationary pressures, and earnings risks. Several stocks gained significantly on company-specific news.
SPY.author: Rishabh Mishra
